use_case: Semiconductor quality event root cause analysis and yield improvement
space_description:
**Subindustry:** Semiconductor

**Use case:** Quality Event Root Cause Analysis & Yield Improvement

NanoVista Semiconductor — fab quality analytics for 20 products across 4 fabs (Taiwan, Arizona, Dresden, Singapore). Yield Engineering and Fab Operations use this space to triage defect excursions, isolate dominant failure modes, and prioritize 8D corrective actions; the Chief Quality Officer and Customer Quality leaders use it to monitor DPPM, containment effectiveness, and customer-impacting escapes.

**Key KPIs**
- Die yield % — average wafer-level good-die rate; leading-edge fabs target 90%+, mature nodes 95%+
- DPPM — defective parts per million shipped; automotive-grade target <10, consumer <500
- First-pass yield % — share of lots passing electrical test without rework; target 90%+
- Defect density per cm² — wafer defectivity; mature processes <0.10, ramping nodes <0.30
- Containment effectiveness % — defects caught before shipment; target 95%+
- Critical event count — Critical-severity excursions per month; trend should be flat or declining
- Mean time to resolution (days) — avg cycle from event open to closure; target <7 days
- Affected wafer count — at-risk WIP per excursion; sizes containment scope

**Data sources**
- `quality_events` — daily quality event records with failure mode, severity, and root cause category
- `manufacturing_lots` — weekly lot snapshots with yield %, lot grade, defect density, and cycle time
- `quality_kpi_monthly` — monthly DPPM, first-pass yield, containment, and customer complaint KPIs

tables.description: Daily quality event records capturing defect types, failure modes, severity levels, root cause categories, and disposition status across fab locations.

columns.name: event_date
columns.comment: Date the quality event was recorded

columns.name: product_family
columns.comment: Product family grouping (PowerLogic, DriveMax, ConnectRF, MemVault, SenseEdge)

columns.name: fab_location
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {status_noise} < 0.30 THEN 'FAB-Taiwan' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.55 THEN 'FAB-Arizona' WHEN {status_noise} < 0.80 THEN 'FAB-Dresden' ELSE 'FAB-Singapore' END

columns.name: event_type
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.18 THEN 'Defect Excursion' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.34 THEN 'Process Deviation' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.48 THEN 'Equipment Alarm' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.60 THEN 'Yield Drop' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.72 THEN 'Customer Return' WHEN {alt_status_noise} < 0.86 THEN 'Incoming Material Fail' ELSE 'Environmental Event' END

columns.name: failure_mode
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.07 THEN 'Open Circuit' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.14 THEN 'Short Circuit' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.20 THEN 'Gate Oxide Breakdown' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.26 THEN 'Electromigration' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.32 THEN 'Hot Carrier Injection' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.38 THEN 'Latch-Up' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.44 THEN 'Metal Bridging' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.50 THEN 'Via Void' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.56 THEN 'Particle Contamination' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.62 THEN 'Pattern Collapse' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.68 THEN 'Delamination' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.74 THEN 'Crack Propagation' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.80 THEN 'Solder Joint Fatigue' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.86 THEN 'Wire Bond Lift' WHEN {alt_status_noise2} < 0.93 THEN 'ESD Damage' ELSE 'Corrosion' END

columns.name: severity_level
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise3} < 0.50 THEN 'Minor' WHEN {alt_status_noise3} < 0.74 THEN 'Major' WHEN {alt_status_noise3} < 0.95 THEN 'Observation' ELSE 'Critical' END

columns.name: root_cause_category
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.14 THEN 'Contamination' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.26 THEN 'Lithography' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.38 THEN 'Etch Variation' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.48 THEN 'CMP Defect' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.58 THEN 'Implant Drift' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.68 THEN 'Equipment Fault' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.78 THEN 'Material Defect' WHEN {alt_status_noise4} < 0.88 THEN 'Operator Error' ELSE 'Environmental' END

columns.name: status
columns.generation_expr: CASE WHEN {alt_status_noise5} < 0.51 THEN 'Closed' WHEN {alt_status_noise5} < 0.68 THEN 'Pending' WHEN {alt_status_noise5} < 0.85 THEN 'Open' ELSE 'In Progress' END

columns.name: affected_wafer_count
columns.comment: Number of wafers affected by the event

genie_instructions:
DOMAIN CONTEXT
This space supports Quality Event Root Cause Analysis for a fabless+IDM semiconductor operation running 20 products across 4 fabs (FAB-Taiwan, FAB-Arizona, FAB-Dresden, FAB-Singapore). Stakeholders include Yield Engineering (defect density, lot grade), Fab Operations (event triage, containment), and the Chief Quality Officer (DPPM, customer complaints, escapes). The dominant failure-mode taxonomy spans electrical (Open/Short, Gate Oxide, EM, HCI), mechanical (Crack, Delamination, Wire Bond Lift), and contamination/process drift (Particle, CMP, Implant).

METRIC DEFINITIONS
- Die yield % = yield_pct (manufacturing_lots); leading-edge target 90%+, mature 95%+
- Defect density = defect_density_per_cm2; target <0.10 mature, <0.30 ramping
- DPPM = dppm (quality_kpi_monthly); automotive <10, industrial <100, consumer <500
- First-pass yield = first_pass_yield_pct; target 90%+
- Containment effectiveness = containment_effectiveness_pct; target 95%+
- Critical events = severity_level = 'Critical' in quality_events
- Resolution cycle = avg_resolution_days; target <7 days
- Lot grade C = yield_pct < 75% (failing lots, must be investigated)

QUERY GUIDANCE
- ALWAYS prefer metric views with MEASURE() syntax for aggregations.
  - quality_events_metrics (source: quality_events) — dims: event_date, product_family, fab_location, root_cause_category, severity_level; measures: total_quality_events, critical_event_count, closed_event_count, total_wafers_affected, open_event_count, unique_product_count, max_affected_wafer_count.
  - lot_yield_metrics (source: manufacturing_lots) — dims: snapshot_date, product_family, fab_location, lot_grade; measures: avg_yield_pct, total_good_die, avg_defect_density, total_lots, grade_c_lot_count, total_cycle_time_hours, unique_product_count, max_yield_percent, total_wafers_in_lot.
- Use GROUP BY ALL with MEASURE() queries.
- For monthly trends, always wrap the date in DATE_TRUNC('month', <date_col>).
- For "Top X" requests, return LIMIT 10 unless the user specifies otherwise.
- Query base tables directly only when needing columns not exposed by metric views (e.g. product_id, product_name, failure_mode, dppm, first_pass_yield_pct, customer_complaints).
- When the user's phrasing matches a SQL snippet display name (filters, expressions, or measures), prefer that snippet.
sample_questions: Which 10 products have the lowest average lot yield over the trailing 12 months?
Show monthly critical event count by fab location for the trailing 12 months.
Which root cause categories account for the most wafers affected this quarter?
Rank product families by average defect density per cm² — which need yield-improvement focus?
How has average DPPM trended monthly across all fabs, and which fab is above the 100 DPPM threshold?
Which products have the highest customer complaint volume in the trailing 6 months, and what is their first-pass yield?
What is the monthly trend in grade C lot count by product family — where is yield slipping below 75%?

example_sqls.question: What is the monthly trend in open event count?
How many distinct transactions appeared each month?
sql_lines: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', event_date) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT transaction) AS distinct_count

example_sqls.question: How many distinct snapshots appeared each month?
sql_lines: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', snapshot_date) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT snapshot) AS distinct_count

example_sqls.question: Which products have the highest total *?
sql_lines: SELECT product_name, SUM(*) AS record_count, SUM(affected_wafer_count) AS total_affected_wafer_count

example_sqls.question: What is the trend of total number of wafers in the lot over time?
sql_lines: GROUP BY snapshot_date ORDER BY snapshot_date

example_sqls.question: How has the average first pass yield percentage changed over time?
sql_lines: GROUP BY kpi_month ORDER BY kpi_month

example_sqls.question: How has open event count changed over time?
